newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Jobbers fuel SAfrica gold shares on better bullion.
newsitem.headline: Jobbers fuel SAfrica gold shares on better bullion.

text.p: Speculators took heart from the better bullion price to snap up South African gold shares on Monday, shoving the index more than five percent higher in the first hour of trade, dealers said.
"People are looking for a quick turn in the market. It's the gamblers and the jobbers. It's purely short-term," one dealer said.
By 0841 GMT the index was 48.8 points higher at 1,013.6 points, but volumes as yet were fairly thin.
But dealers said it would take more than the bullion price holding these levels to fuel further rises in gold shares and they saw shares coming off later in the day.

"It will need to do more than just hold. More than likely there will be a bit of profit-taking later. The shares won't go higher unless there is a further big upward movement in the gold price," one dealer said.
Gold opened firmer in Europe and dealers there said it was likely to drift higher despite long-term bearish sentiment.
Gold was last at $321.60/322.10 an ounce.
But South African dealers said that possible central bank gold sales still clouded the market and would continue to pose a threat to the metal price.
They said local gold shares were being bought by speculators who would take a quick profit and that other investors were likely to remain cautious for a while yet.

"The central bank issue is a fairly big negative. It's a big threat to the market and won't be forgotten. If any other sales take place the sentiment will be so blue, the gold market won't have a chance," one dealer said.
The bullion price slid to 12-year lows on July 2 after news the Australian central bank had sold 167 tonnes of its gold reserves over the last six months.
South African gold shares took a bashing last week in the wake of the metal's slide and touched a four-year low of 898.2 points on July 7.
Gold shares featuring on Monday included Western Areas which surged 275 cents to 31.75 rand, Western Deep which climbed 700 cents to 110 rand and Avgold which rose 33 cents to 475 cents.
ERPM saw some good volumes with 613,400 shares changing hands so far. IT was last two cents higher at 120 cents.
The world's biggest gold mine Freegold added 70 cents to 23.50 rand.
